title: DriveSpeed disk test report
print_hint: In the print dialog, choose Save as PDF.
unknown_eta: Remaining time cannot yet be estimated
cache_limit: This bounded run does not establish speed after SSD cache exhaustion or explain thermal throttling.
sensors_limit: Temperature, SMART and negotiated link speed are unavailable unless separately collected. No cause is inferred from a slowdown alone.
method_text: File-based I/O only. direct=1 requests OS cache bypass; device cache remains. Write tests use end_fsync. MB/s = 1,000,000 bytes/s. QD is requested; achieved depth is recorded separately.
privacy: Public HTML hides full paths and serial numbers. Raw local files may contain private paths; review before sharing.
raw: Raw results are stored beside this report.
sample: Synthetic fixture — not a drive measurement
dependency_failed: fio installation or identity verification failed
unsupported: Platform or device is not supported
trash_note: Test files were moved to Trash. Space is not reclaimed until Trash is emptied.
retain_note: Test files retained. See results.json for the exact owned directory.
pdf_failed: Automatic PDF export unavailable; open HTML and use Download PDF.
recovery: Review local logs and rerun only after fixing the cause.
analysis_hint: Compare the workload relevant to your use. Repeat with the same cable, port and load to investigate differences; do not infer device health from benchmark scores.
tail_mean: Average write speed at test end
window_method: Initial: first 5 s. Tail: final third, capped at 30 s. Slowdown candidate: 10 consecutive samples below 70% of initial speed, after 5 s. This identifies a speed change, not a cache boundary. Cache exhaustion remains unconfirmed. No SNIA conformance or steady-state claim.
footer_method: Method references: fio and SNIA; not a conformance test
partial_write: Incomplete run: total written bytes unknown; recorded lower bound
bridge_candidates: Detected bridge candidates (not associated with this target)
enclosure_unknown: Retail enclosure model unconfirmed; a controller ID is not an enclosure model.
skill_intro: Test an internal or external drive safely and read the measured results.
cache_capacity: Available write cache in this run (estimate)
cache_no_drop: No continuous slowdown meeting the detection criteria was identified, so cache capacity and post-cache speed remain unconfirmed. This does not mean speed stayed unchanged. The interface may also mask cache differences.
cache_waiting: A slowdown was observed, but a stable 60-second window after it is still missing.
cache_stable: A stable 60-second window after slowdown was recorded. Cache capacity and post-cache speed are estimates for this run; the cause of slowdown is not independently confirmed.
cache_incomplete: Cache measurement is incomplete: budget, time limit or interruption stopped the test before a stable post-drop window.
cache_sampling: Samples are insufficient, discontinuous, or the initial speed is unstable. Cache cannot yet be estimated.
cache_method: Cache observation detects at least 10 seconds below 70% of initial speed, continues for 30 seconds, then requires a stable 60-second window. Window variation and fitted trend change must each stay within 10% of its mean. Cache size is estimated from bytes written before slowdown; post-cache speed is the window weighted mean. The cause is not independently confirmed.
tail_explanation: Average write speed at test end uses samples covering the final third of the write log, capped at 30 seconds, weighted by each sample duration; the boundary sample is included in full. It describes the end of this test, not verified post-cache speed.
reference_conditions: Ratings and other test conditions are shown separately from this run; no compliance percentage is calculated. Gb/s is link bandwidth; MB/s is file throughput.
large_file_use: Large files: videos, archives and model files
large_file_result: The sequential test measured reads at {read} and writes at {write}.
file_time_example: For 10 GB, that translates to about {read_time} of pure reading or {write_time} of pure writing.
small_file_use: Small scattered accesses: project files and indexes
small_file_result: With one request at a time to scattered 4 KiB blocks, reads measured {read} and writes {write}. This is different work from large sequential transfers, so the two MB/s figures are not directly comparable.
latency_example: In this test, 95% of small read requests completed their I/O wait within {latency}; application overhead is separate.
scenario_limits: File times are calculations from this run, not copy-test results. Real copying also depends on the other drive, filesystem and cache; small-block results are not application launch times.
same_run_comparison: Within this run: one request versus a deeper queue
comparison_limits: Only matched tests on this device with the same block size are shown. Ratios describe throughput, not application speedups. Actual queue depth, duration and temperature are in the full data.
guide_speed_text: Higher is faster for the same access pattern and conditions. 1000 MB is about 1 GB. Sequential results are most relevant to large transfers.
guide_iops_text: Useful for small-block access. Compare only matching block sizes; random tests here use 4 KiB blocks.
guide_latency: Latency: the wait for an operation
guide_latency_text: µs means microseconds; 1000 µs = 1 ms. p50 / p95 / p99 are the times within which 50% / 95% / 99% of requests completed their I/O wait. They exclude total application time.
guide_queue: QD: requests allowed in the queue
guide_queue_text: QD1 allows at most one request at a time; QD16 allows up to 16. More queuing may improve throughput and increase each request’s wait. Reads use only the region already covered by writes.
lowest_known_limit: {direction}: lowest known reference; actual bottleneck unconfirmed
reference_headroom: Rated above the lowest known reference
reference_unknown_constraint: Unknown; may impose a lower limit
path_minimum_rule: The path uses the lowest reference for the computer port, enclosure and drive, including confirmed controller limits. 1 Gb/s = 125 MB/s before protocol overhead.
path_partial: References are incomplete. This minimum uses known stages only; a missing stage may impose a lower limit. The actual bottleneck is not established.
path_rated_only: This is a theoretical reference from known official ratings, not a speed this run must reach. Protocol overhead, negotiated rate and device state still matter.
path_gap_explanation: The gap is an arithmetic difference, not directly recoverable performance or proof of a bottleneck. A measurement above the reference calls for checking sources, units and conditions.
controller_fallback: Enclosure specifications unconfirmed; use the confirmed controller rating as a reference. Actual enclosure capability remains unknown.
cache_summary_note: Write cache is a temporary fast landing area. Online sizes apply to specific conditions; availability here depends on free space, earlier writes and cache recovery. Not measured does not mean no cache.
cache_difference_review: The cache estimate differs from the nearest online reference by {percent}%; review required. The 30% threshold is a report triage rule, not an industry failure standard. Check capacity variant, free space, cache recovery, connection, temperature and method, then retest under comparable conditions.
peak_title: Peak, average and host interface ceiling
peak_note: Peak is the highest fio bandwidth log sample (configured for roughly 1-second averages), not an instantaneous maximum. Mean uses total bytes and runtime. Short tests have sparse logs and an uncovered tail, so the logged peak may be slightly below the mean. The host value converts official rated bandwidth before protocol overhead; it is not a file-transfer target. Percentages are numerical comparisons, not interface utilization or pass rates, and do not identify the bottleneck.
short_group_note: One outstanding request. Each value is the mean of its own test.
mapping_note: Random access across increasing address ranges; the second pass repeats the same sequence. This measures whole-device behavior, not DRAM capacity or its isolated contribution.
integrity_pass: Verified test region; physical spare blocks and existing files are not covered.
integrity_incomplete: Verification incomplete or failed; inspect raw errors before drawing a hardware conclusion.
recovery_comparison: Recovery comparison (MB/s): initial / end / after idle
recovery_note: Idle recovery includes both cooling and internal cache maintenance; it does not isolate either cause.
translation_promo: A Chrome translation extension for your PDFs—free, private, and fast.
link_encoded: after link encoding; before protocol overhead
link_unknown: Target-associated link speed is unavailable. No interface generation is inferred from measured speed.
link_scope: Each row describes one link segment, not the full path or a guaranteed file speed. Rated capability and current negotiation are different. USB-C is a connector shape.
rating_scope: Levels 1–5 describe this metric against source-backed bands under matched conditions. They do not establish authenticity, quality or health. Missing evidence is left unscored.
interface_catalog: Interface reference bounds (not throughput pass marks)
rating_post_cache_mb_s: Stable speed after observed write slowdown
rating_reason_conditions_unknown: Hardware path or comparison conditions are incomplete.
rating_reason_reference_missing: No matching source-backed five-level reference; a rated peak alone is insufficient.
rating_reason_reference_stale: Reference date is missing, future-dated or older than 30 days. Recheck its source.
rating_reason_above_reference_range: Above the documented reference range. Check cache, units and method; no quality conclusion.
rating_reason_above_link_bound: Above a known link bound. Check units, cache and link metadata before interpreting the result.
util_scope: Complete QD16 sequential read and write are divided by their respective capacities and averaged. Stars increase at 20%, 40%, 60% and 80%. These are project display bands; fewer stars do not imply poor quality. With one direction available only that direction is used. Signal rates exclude full protocol overhead and do not guarantee file throughput. Random I/O and post-slowdown writes are separate. Exceeding a reference by 10% or using less than 40% of the weakest known path prompts checking, not a fault or authenticity verdict.
util_comment_high: Data exceeds a known reference; retest and check caching, units and hardware information.
util_comment_low: Performance is well below known path capacity; retest and check the connection, temperature and background activity.
util_comment_incomplete: Complete the hardware specifications and sequential tests to assess the configuration.
util_comment_balanced: Known component capacities are close; this run appears balanced.
util_comment_bottleneck: The {component} is the likely limiting component.
util_comment_normal: The run is below known path limits; check test conditions before upgrading.
util_comment_measurement_quality: Background conditions are unknown or affected by activity; this run is not used for device ratings or bottleneck attribution. Resolve interference and restore background monitoring before measuring again. Keep this result local; do not submit it.
quality_quiet_observed: No other disk activity observed in two 5-second pre-run windows; not a whole-run guarantee.
quality_interference_observed: Attributed activity observed before the run; results describe this host path under those conditions.
quality_visibility_limited: Pre-run activity attribution or visibility was limited; device-only attribution is unavailable.
quality_unknown: Historical measurement conditions were not recorded.
rating_reason_measurement_quality: Background conditions do not qualify for device-only attribution.
confirm_write: Authorize this finite disk write plan? Type RUN to confirm:
core_incomplete: Core measurements or required logs are incomplete. This is a partial result and cannot be submitted as a complete report.
incomplete_measurement: Required measurements or collection are incomplete.
sampling_irregular: Sampling scheduling was uneven, limiting time resolution. Final statistics are retained; fixed-window and cache conclusions are not provided.
depth_raw: Achieved depth distribution (fio values, not normalized)
